key_insight: A forked physics-informed neural network separates simulation and control objectives at the gradient level, enabling stable joint optimization for non-Markovian open quantum dynamics.
engineering_relevance: This provides an end-to-end differentiable framework for quantum simulation and control that can improve state preparation fidelity while producing smoother, more experimentally practical pulses.
method: Add a dedicated control branch to the existing FPINN architecture.
Use selective gradient flow to decouple conflicting optimization objectives.
Jointly train the network to fit open-system dynamics and control targets without compromising either task.
evidence_signal: On a two-qubit Heisenberg XXX model, the method reproduces non-Markovian features such as decoherence and information backflow and achieves higher state-preparation fidelity than GAP, chopped random basis, and standard PINNs.
watch_item: Performance may depend on careful gradient-branch design and training stability, especially as the system/environment becomes more dissipative or closer to Markovian behavior.
paper_title: Forked Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Non-Markovian Open Quantum Dynamics and Control
